title: Citi Bars AI Agent Account Access to Help Protect $1.6T Deposit Base
summary:
Citigroup has prohibited external software assistants from logging into customer accounts or executing monetary transfers within its digital banking platforms, the Financial Times reports. The lender joins JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America in restricting third party AI agents, with JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon previously warning that thousands of rogue agents could potentially operate inside the bank if such limits were not imposed.

The restrictions aim to prevent automated tools from shifting client funds from low-interest checking accounts, which pay about 0.1%, to fintech alternatives offering 3.3% to 5%. JPMorgan, Bank of America and Wells Fargo hold $1.6T in non-interest deposits, and banks could face annual costs of $47B to pay 3% interest on those funds, an amount nearly equal to half of their combined yearly earnings.
